title: Polynomial-time solution of simple stochastic games
decision_reason: Sourced exact formulation, independent corroboration, nine source/scope audits, current searches, duplicate checks, separated A68 self-review and final rendering/link/structural checks passed.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Finite explicitly encoded directed simple graph G=(V,E), partitioned into Max, Min, random vertices and exactly two sinks 0,1. Every nonsink has two outgoing edges; every vertex has a graph path to at least one sink. Designated nonsink start o.
problem_fingerprint.dynamics: At each visited Max/Min vertex that player chooses the successor. At a random vertex a fresh independent fair coin chooses one of the two successors. All states and past moves are observed.
problem_fingerprint.strategies: Pure positional sigma and tau choose one outgoing edge at each vertex of the corresponding player. Optimal such strategies exist even among history-dependent randomized strategies.
problem_fingerprint.observable: v(o)=max_sigma min_tau Pr_o^{sigma,tau}(eventually hit sink 1). Reaching sink 0 or traversing forever without sink 1 has payoff zero.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: One deterministic algorithm and absolute constants C,c>0 deciding v(o)>1/2 on every input in at most C(L+1)^c Turing-machine steps, where L is its finite adjacency-list bit length.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Unbounded numbers of all three vertex types; exact decision including v(o)=1/2 as no; no probabilistic algorithm, gap promise, fixed parameter, ladder structure, or almost-sure stopping promise.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Canonical binary reachability decision problem of GHH26 section 2.2. The underlying graph-path assumption does not ensure absorption for every strategy pair.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One stochastic reachability complexity family. Value/strategy computation and related payoff-game reductions are contextual; no separate count for parameters, aliases or restricted graphs.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Strongly polynomial feasible simplex pivots for an LP; here any polynomial-bit-time decision algorithm for an adversarial reachability game is eligible.
Fixed scalar decentralized Gaussian control optimum with unequal information; here variable finite-state perfect-information zero-sum reachability complexity.
Decidability of exact hyperplane reachability for a deterministic real-time linear ODE; no adversarial players or probability threshold.
Unrestricted-time decidability of asymptotic stability under all matrix switching sequences; not polynomial-time finite-graph stochastic reachability.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Enumeration of random-vertex permutations gives a factorial parameter bound.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The number of random vertices is unbounded in the target; fixed-parameter tractability is insufficient. The improvement variant's possible polynomial runtime is left unproved.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Deterministic O(phi^m Poly(L)), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, m the number of Max vertices.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This bound is exponential in an input parameter. It is historical progress, not claimed to be the latest general bound.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Deterministic SSG runtime L^{O(sqrt(n) log n)} for n vertices.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: A dimension-dependent exponent does not give one polynomial bound valid for all inputs. Query efficiency alone also does not control computation between queries.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial algorithm for stopping binary SSGs on ladders.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The target permits arbitrary level sizes and strategy pairs that fail to terminate. A stopping transformation need not preserve ladder structure.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Reduction of stopping half-threshold games to exact SDP feasibility.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This supplies a reduction, not a solver for its target. Approximate numerical SDP methods do not automatically decide exact feasibility; §1 expressly leaves feasibility outside known P. Their nonstrict threshold convention is recorded, not treated as the decisive obstacle.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Improved Tarski query bounds in fixed dimension.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Dimension varies with game size, and the exponent grows with dimension. No uniform polynomial bit-time game algorithm follows.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Convergent lower and upper value bounds, stopping at any supplied positive interval width.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Finite-precision termination does not itself supply a polynomial exact threshold decider. No polynomial worst-case bound in input length and required precision is proved here.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial SSG decision conditional on feasible interpolation for the stated Frege systems.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The extra proof-complexity hypothesis is not established by this theorem; it is not an unconditional algorithm.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Repairing a winning strategy through a quotient of a two-player deterministic reachability game.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Every vertex belongs to one of the players; there are no random transitions. Randomly generated experimental instances do not create stochastic game dynamics. The theorem lifts a quotient solution and does not solve the quantitative stochastic target.

independent_corroboration.statement: GHH26 supplies the exact binary strict-threshold formulation; GH09 and HP11 explicitly pose the polynomial-time problem.
independent_corroboration.current_independent_assessment: CLY26 is an independently authored March 2026 specialist assessment. GHH26 was published May 15, 2026. Current searches were actually executed September 19.

independent_corroboration.original_access: Condon 1992 was not read in full. The 1993 author PDF had garbled extracted text and was not relied upon as a read original. Explicit accessible scholarly restatements supply Gate A.

normalization_checks: Vertex counts and graph bit length are input variables; one fixed exponent must work for every instance.
Two sinks, fair independent random choices, perfect information, turn-based moves, infinite-horizon reachability.
No almost-sure absorption or promise separating the value from one half.
Optimal pure positional strategies exist; a fixed strategy pair can be evaluated but enumerating pairs need not be polynomial.
One canonical game family; restricted graphs and payoff reductions are not additional entries.
Fixed-epsilon approximation can support exact computation only with adequate precision and runtime control; neither is silently assumed.
